message.content:
LeBron James is an American professional basketball player widely regarded as one of the greatest athletes in the history of the sport. Born on December 30, 1984, in Akron, Ohio, he played high school basketball at St. Vincent‑St. Mary High School, where he gained national attention and was named the USA Today High School Player of the Year.

He entered the NBA directly from high school, being selected first overall by the Cleveland Cavaliers in the 2003 draft. LeBron quickly became a dominant force in the league, earning the NBA Rookie of the Year award in 2004. Over his career, he has played for the Cleveland Cavaliers (two stints), the Miami Heat, and the Los Angeles Lakers.

Key highlights of his career include:

- **NBA Championships**: Four titles (2007 with the Cavaliers, 2012 & 2013 with the Heat, 2020 with the Lakers).
- **MVP Awards**: Four regular‑season MVPs (2009, 2010, 2012, 2013) and one Finals MVP (2012).
- **All‑Star Appearances**: 19 selections, including multiple All‑NCAA teams.
- **Scoring and Playmaking**: Known for his combination of size, athleticism, and basketball IQ, LeBron has consistently posted high averages in points, rebounds, and assists.

Beyond the court, LeBron is also known for his philanthropy, notably the LeBron James Family Foundation, which opened the “I Promise School” in Akron to support at-risk youth. He has also pursued acting, producing, and business ventures, making him a prominent figure in both sports and popular culture.
